zh: 阿尔弗雷德·盖尔于1997年1月辞世，他被广泛视为同代社会人类学家中最富才华者之一。他的写作与思想严谨而富于分析性，却又时常诙谐而富有挑战性；无论是社会理论中最一般性的议题，还是仪式、实践与人工制品中最繁复的细节，他都能同样娴熟地加以处理。这些能力在本书中得到了充分体现，而本书或许堪称艺术人类学这一研究领域诞生以来最激进的一次重新思考。本书无疑将大量抽象的模型建构，与对具体艺术对象和艺术风格极具洞见的讨论结合在了一起。
en: Alfred Gell, who died in January 1997, was widely regarded as one of the most brilliant social anthropologists of his generation. His writing and thought were rigorously analytical, yet often also playful and provocative; he was equally deft in engaging the most general issues of social theory, and the most intricate elements of rituals, practices, and artefacts. These capacities are exemplified in this book, which may amount to the most radical rethinking of the anthropology of art since that field of inquiry emerged. The book certainly combines a good deal of abstract model-making with remarkably insightful discussions of particular art objects and art styles.

zh: 然而，尽管本书行文清晰直白，却未必易于把握。这里必须承认，倘若作者天假以年，他必定还会做进一步的工作；他确实留下了一些修订笔记，只是来不及付诸实施。我们手上这部书是一份完整的草稿，其中大部分仅在一个月左右的时间内写就，而非一个经过充分打磨的定本。不过应当补充的是，阿尔弗雷德·盖尔的论文与著作大多成形良好；他写作时极为投入，但偏好在思路从头到尾都已清晰成形之后才动笔。因此可以说，本书已接近他预期的最终形态，只是尚欠润饰；倘若盖尔有机会，书中某些有力的段落本会加以限定，某些论点本会增补或展开，某些章节本会与全书更好地融为一体。
en: Yet, despite it being written in a lucid and direct way, it is not necessarily an easy book to grasp. It does need to be acknowledged here that, had the author lived longer, he would certainly have done further work; he indeed left notes toward revisions that he did not have the time to carry out. What we have is the full draft of a book, most of which was written over a period of only a month, not an absolutely refined version. It should be added, though, that Alfred Gell's essays and books did, for the most part, emerge well formed; he wrote with great intensity, but preferred to write when his ideas were clearly worked out, from start to finish. The book can therefore be said to approximate an intended final form, but it does lack polishing, and there are certainly forceful passages that would have been qualified, points that would have added or elaborated, and sections that would have been better integrated with the whole, had Gell had the opportunity.

zh: 本书尤其欠缺的，是一篇能够简明预示其整体论证的序言或导论。我虽对概括另一位学者的著作心存犹豫，也坦率地怀疑自己是否有能力公正对待一个复杂而盘曲的论证的各个层面，但我认为这正是本前言应当尝试去做的，以便让随后的论证更易于理解，尤其是对那些不熟悉阿尔弗雷德·盖尔其他著作的读者而言。本书建立在若干论文的基础之上，读过《魅惑技术与技术的魅惑》（1992b）、《福格尔之网：作为艺术品的陷阱与作为陷阱的艺术品》（1996），或盖尔研究波利尼西亚纹身的《以影像包裹》（1993）的人类学家，将能预见到本书所取的方向。
en: What the book lacks, in particular, is a preface or introduction proper, that concisely foreshadows its overall argument. While I hesitate to summarize another scholar's book, and am frankly unsure of my capacity to do justice to the various dimensions of a complex and involved argument, I believe that this is what this foreword should attempt, in order to make the arguments that follow more accessible, particularly to readers unfamiliar with Alfred Gell's other work. This book builds on a number of essays, and anthropologists who have read ‘The Technology of Enchantment and the Enchantment of Technology' (1992b), ‘Vogel's Net: Traps as Artworks and Artworks as Traps' (1996), or Gell's study of Polynesian tattooing, Wrapping in Images (1993), will anticipate the directions that it takes.

zh: 其中，《魅惑技术》一文尤其预示了本书的若干主要论点。在那篇文章里，盖尔挑衅性地宣称，艺术人类学迄今为止几乎毫无进展，因为它未能把自己与审美欣赏的事业区分开来——后者之于艺术，恰如神学之于宗教。他主张，如果这门学科要转而采取一种类似于宗教社会学的立场，就需要一种与社会学的“方法论无神论”相当的方法论上的“非利士主义”。这就要求摒弃人类学家作为有教养的中产阶级知识分子通常所信奉的“艺术崇拜”。然而，这并非要倡导一种去魅的社会学分析，去指认艺术在维系阶级文化或为支配性意识形态提供合法性方面的作用：盖尔认为，这类进路未能触及艺术对象本身，未能触及它们的特殊性与效力。更具体地说，他对艺术界制度所提出的问题相对不感兴趣，转而相信艺术人类学应当考察艺术的一般运作方式。
en: The essay on ‘The Technology of Enchantment', in particular, foreshadows some of the larger arguments here. In that paper, Gell provocatively claimed that the anthropology of art had got virtually nowhere thus far, because it had failed to dissociate itself from projects of aesthetic appreciation, that are to art as theology is to religion. He argued that if the discipline was instead to adopt the position analogous to that of the sociology of religion, it needed a methodological philistinism equivalent to sociology's methodological atheism. This required disowning the ‘art cult' to which anthropologists, as cultured middleclass intellectuals, generally subscribe. This was not, however, to advocate a demystifying sociological analysis that would identify the role of art in sustaining class cultures, or in legitimizing dominant ideologies: Gell suggested that approaches of this kind failed to engage with art objects themselves, with their specificity and efficacy. More particularly, he was relatively uninterested in the questions raised by art world institutions, believing instead that the anthropology of art should address the workings of art in general.

zh: 他提出，可以把艺术视为一种特殊形式的技术，尤其是把艺术对象视为某种装置——“用以确保个体默从于他们身陷其中的意向性之网”（1992b: 43）——从而在不屈从于这些对象的魅力与光晕的前提下，处理艺术对象的效力问题。举例来说，特罗布里恩德船首板（巴布亚新几内亚马辛地区）那种极其繁复套叠、摄人心魄的形式，就在竞争性交换的情境中发挥着一种心理战的作用。这些船首板面对交换伙伴的东道主，理想的效果是使其目眩、使其着迷、使其困惑，从而让他们以低于实际价值的代价交出贵重之物——即人类学著名的库拉贝壳。不过，这一主张并非还原论的：它并不是说对象本身在某种意义上独自做到了这一点，或将独立于一个期待与理解的场域而做到这一点；在这个例子中，正是这一场域以人们已知渗入其制作过程的魔力包裹了这件人工制品。技术之所以魅惑人心，是因为它本身已被施魅，因为它是某种几乎不可理解的精湛技艺的产物，而这种技艺体现了人们在其他领域竭力实现的巫术效力的理想状态。
en: He proposed that it was possible to address questions of the efficacy of the art object, without succumbing to the fascination and aura of those objects, by taking art as a special form of technology, and especially by regarding art objects as devices ‘for securing the acquiescence of individuals in the network of intentionalities in which they are enmeshed' (1992b: 43). For example, brilliantly involuted and captivating forms such as those of Trobriand prowboards (of the Massim region, Papua New Guinea) work a kind of psychological warfare, in a situation of competitive exchange. These boards confront the hosts of exchange partners, ideally dazzle them, beguile them, and confuse them, leading them to surrender their valuables-anthropology's famous kula shells-for less than their value. The claim here is not reductive, however: it is not suggested that in some sense the object by itself does this, or would do it, independently of a field of expectations and understandings, which in this case envelope the artefact with magical prowess, which is known to have entered into its making. Technology is enchanting because it is enchanted, because it is the outcome of some process of barely comprehensible virtuosity, that exemplifies an ideal of magical efficacy that people struggle to realize in other domains.

zh: 1992年的那篇文章有一处小的不一致：它似乎假定艺术人类学仍然是对“原始”艺术的研究（盖尔拒绝“非西方”这一委婉用语，理由是它把东方高级艺术及其他传统也包括在内，而这些显然具有与经典部落艺术形式截然不同的社会位置）。然而，他随后用来说明艺术对象的“技术难度的光环效应”及其他方面的例子，却包括了美国错视画家J. F. 皮托和毕加索的绘画。他的理论实际上可能是一种关于一切艺术之运作的理论，而非仅仅关于据称是特定人群所特有的艺术的理论——这一暗示正是本书的一个前提。
en: There was a minor inconsistency in the 1992 article, in the sense that it seemed to be assumed that the anthropology of art remained the study of ‘primitive' art (Gell rejected the euphemistic term ‘non-Western' on the grounds that this included high Oriental art and other traditions, which clearly possessed an entirely different social location to the canonical tribal art forms). However, the examples he proceeded to use, in pointing to the ‘halo effect of technical difficulty' and other aspects of the art objects, included the paintings of the American illusionist J. F. Peto, and Picasso. The implication that his theory might in fact be a theory of the workings of all art, rather than that supposedly characteristic of particular populations, is a premiss of the present book.

zh: 最初几章是对1992年那篇文章论证的一次引人注目的展开。盖尔首先承认，从更广泛的文化与政治角度看，承认非西方审美体系的独特性是可取的，但他断言这不能构成一种“人类学的”理论，理由是人类学理论本质上关注的是社会关系，是在生命史的时间尺度上展开的社会关系。正如他所承认的，这种定义取向可能引发争议，但它可以说为这一特定研究提供了一个富有成效的出发点。有两条彼此关联的理由，说明为何应当离开跨文化美学的进路。其一，许多经典的部落艺术品，例如新几内亚西南部的阿斯马特盾牌，显然不是为了唤起常规意义上的“审美”欣赏——它们毋宁说在猎头活动的致命心理战中扮演了角色，而这种猎头活动在“平定”之前是阿斯马特社会性的根本所在。其二，是对众多符号学与象征论艺术理论所调用的语言学类比的断然拒绝。这或许正是本书最激进之处。对许多学者而言，乃至在关于艺术的许多常识性思考中，艺术关乎意义与沟通乃是一条公理。本书则提出，艺术关乎的是“做”。
en: The first chapters amount to a dramatic elaboration of the arguments of the 1992 essay. Gell begins by deferring to the desirability, in broader cultural and political terms, of acknowledging the distinctness of non-Western aesthetic systems, but asserts that this cannot constitute an ‘anthropological' theory, on the grounds that anthropological theories are essentially concerned with social relations, over the time-frame of biographies. As he acknowledges, this definitional orientation may be contentious, but it arguably provides a productive departure point for this particular inquiry. There are two linked arguments for a shift away from cross-cultural aesthetics. The first is that many canonical pieces of tribal art, such as the Asmat shields of south-west New Guinea, are plainly not intended to elicit ‘aesthetic' appreciation in the conventional sense-they rather had a part to play in the deadly psychological warfare of headhunting, that was so fundamental to Asmat sociality before pacification. The second is a categorical rejection of the linguistic analogies that have been mobilized by so many semiotic and symbolic theories of art. And this is perhaps the sense in which this book is most radical. For many scholars, and indeed in much common-sense thinking about art, it is axiomatic that art is a matter of meaning and communication. This book suggests that it is instead about doing.

zh: “做”被理论化为能动性，被理论化为一个涉及索引与效应的过程；艺术人类学由此被建构为一种能动性理论，或者说一种关于能动性如何经由索引而中介的理论——索引在此仅被理解为激发推断、反应或解释的物质实体。索引与原型、艺术家、接受者处于种种关系之中。原型是索引可能再现或代表的事物，例如肖像中所描绘的人——尽管事物也可以以非摹仿的、非视觉的方式被“再现”。接受者是索引被认为对其产生作用的人，或者在某些情况下自身也能经由索引而发挥作用的人（一幅由庄园主人委托绘制的乡村庄园景致，可能更多是接受者自我颂扬的能动性的载体，而非艺术家的能动性的载体）。艺术家是被认为对索引的存在及其特征负有直接因果责任的人，但正如我们刚才指出的，他们可能是他人能动性的载体，而非西方常识观念与艺术界理论中那种自足的、创造性的行动者。在这方面值得注意的是，尽管本书的风格与取向同玛丽琳·斯特拉森在美拉尼西亚研究中采用的解构论进路（1988；另见 Wagner 1992）存在显著差异，盖尔却可以说完全接受了斯特拉森关于“可分的”或“分布式”人格的概念，并且确实阐明了从这一概念如何推出：行动及其效应同样不是各自独立的个体意志表达，而是中介性实践的结果，施动者与受动者以复杂的方式牵涉其中。一方面，艺术家的能动性很少是自足的；另一方面，索引也不仅仅是行动的“产物”或终点，而是一个施动者的分布式延展。波尔布特的一名士兵以地雷的形式分布自身效力的诸要素，这个令人不寒而栗的例子，是众多出人意料却又贴切的实例之一，它使这些术语原本可能艰涩抽象的阐述获得了某种具体性。
en: ‘Doing' is theorized as agency, as a process involving indexes and effects; the anthropology of art is constructed as a theory of agency, or of the mediation of agency by indexes, understood simply as material entities which motivate inferences, responses or interpretations. Indexes stand in a variety of relations to prototypes, artists, and recipients. Prototypes are the things that indices may represent or stand for, such as the person depicted in a portrait-though things may be ‘represented' non-mimetically, and non-visually. Recipients are those whom indexes are taken to effect, or who may, in some cases, be effective themselves via the index (a view of a country estate commissioned by the landowner may be a vehicle of the recipient's self-celebrating agency, more than that of the artist. Artists are those who are considered to be immediately causally responsible for the existence and characteristics of index, but as we have just noted, they may be vehicles of the agency of others, not the self-subsistent, creative agents of Western commonsense ideas and art-world theory. In this respect, it is worth noting that despite the notable differences between the style and orientation of this book, and the Melanesianist deconstructionism of Marilyn Strathern (1988; see also Wagner 1992), Gell could be seen to fully embrace Strathern's notion of the ‘partible' or ‘distributed' person, and indeed to make explicit the ways in which it follows from this concept that actions and their effects are similarly not discrete expressions of individual will, but rather the outcomes of mediated practices in which agents and patients are implicated in complex ways. On the one hand the agency of the artist is rarely selfsufficient; on the other the index is not simply a ‘product' or end-point of action, but rather a distributed extension of an agent. The chilling example of one of Pol Pot's soldiers, who distributes elements of his own efficacy in the form of landmines, is one of the many unexpected, yet apt instances that gives what would otherwise be an intractable, abstract exposition of these terms, some concreteness.

zh: 这一理论在第6章和第7章得到了更持续的例证，这两章分别讨论“装饰”艺术与“再现”艺术的形式。前者讨论辟邪图案，即那些旨在使危险的精灵着迷并将其驱避的套叠图案；借助阿斯马特盾牌之类的例子，这些或许最明显地体现了本书的一项主要论点，即艺术对象中介着一种用以达成某些目的的技术，尤其是使受动者陷入施动者所追求或所规定的关系与意向性之中。为避免这显得是一种对艺术的还原论进路——一种本质上把对象视为策略载体的进路——必须强调，艺术品所展现的形式复杂性乃至技术上的精湛技艺，对论证而言并非附带之物，而是绝对核心的。事实上，对该理论至关重要的是，索引展现出“某种认知上的不可解读性”，它们撩拨人，使那些无法立刻辨认“整体与部分、连续与断裂、共时与接续”的观者感到挫败。尽管本书很少进行持续的认知理论化，但在这一点及其他地方值得注意的是，对认知过程的观察推动了盖尔的论证，其程度在人类学中已属罕见。
en: The theory receives more sustained exemplification in Chapters 6 and 7, which address forms of ‘decorative' and ‘representational' art respectively. The first discusses apotropaic patterns, involuted designs intended to entrance and ward off dangerous spirits; with examples such as the Asmat shield, these perhaps manifest most obviously one of the book's larger theses, namely that art objects mediate a technology to achieve certain ends, notably to enmesh patients in relations and intentionalities sought or prescribed by agents. Lest this appear a reductive approach to art, one that takes objects essentially as vehicles of strategies, it is important to emphasize that the formal complexity, and indeed the technical virtuosity, exhibited in works of art is not incidental to the argument but absolutely central to it. It is crucial to the theory, in fact, that indexes display ‘a certain cognitive indecipherability', that they tantalize, they frustrate the viewer unable to recognize at once ‘wholes and parts, continuity and discontinuity, synchrony and succession'. Even though this book engages in little sustained cognitive theorizing, it is notable at this point and elsewhere that cognitive observations animate Gell's argument, to a degree that has become unusual in anthropology.

zh: 随后这一长章广泛论及偶像崇拜、巫术、仪式与人格，并顺带展示了盖尔对范围庞杂得令人眼花缭乱的南亚与波利尼西亚材料的掌握，但它与前面各节的主张完全一致。偶像对本书确实具有特殊意义，因为它们以显著而有力的方式代表着一个施动者或受动者（在巫术的情形中），代表着人或神。它们是能以种种方式被赋予生命的索引，使致命效力、丰产、吉祥等方面的交易成为可能。这里所涉及的能动性与意图的特定形式，以及使偶像成为圣物的过程，都得到了细致探讨。更一般的论点是，对象之中蕴含着能动性的多重牵连，对象与实际的人类施动者之间存在“一种不可分离的过渡”。一旦被作为能动性的索引来理解，有像对象尤其能够在人类社会能动性的网络中占据几乎与人类本身同等的位置。
en: The long chapter which follows ranges widely over idolatry, sorcery, ritual, and personhood, and incidentally displays Gell's grasp of a bewildering range of south Asian and Polynesian source material, but is fully consistent with the claims of the previous sections. Idols are indeed of special relevance for the book, because they stand for an agent or patient (in the case of sorcery), for persons or deities, in manifest and powerful ways. They are indices that may be animated in a variety of ways, that enable transactions in lethal effect, fertility, auspiciousness, and the like. The particular forms of agency and intention at issue here, and the process of consecration, are explored in detail. The larger point is that there are multiple implications of agency in objects, ‘an inseparable transition' between them and actual human agents. Once appreciated as indexes of agency, iconic objects in particular can occupy positions in the networks of human social agency that are almost equivalent to the positions of humans themselves.

zh: 到此为止，盖尔的理论化与例证一直聚焦于特定对象或索引在特定行动中的作用，聚焦于具体过程而非艺术品的整体组合。他在第7章结尾承认，在许多重要的方面，艺术品并非作为单一实体出现，而是作为组合体出现。本书其余部分似乎陡然偏离了迄今受到如此集中关注的施动者与索引范式。它处理艺术品之间的亲缘关系问题，并在处理风格概念时似乎回到了常规立场。然而，这一讨论——它经由对德国民族学家卡尔·冯·登·施泰因所记录的大批非凡的马克萨斯艺术作品所作的细致形式分析而展开——最终与前面的内容是一致的。
en: Up to this point, Gell's theorizing and exemplification have focused upon the work of particular objects or indexes in particular actions, on specific processes rather than entire repertoires of artworks. He concludes Chapter 7 by acknowledging that there are many vital respects in which artworks do not appear as singular entities, but rather as ensembles. The remainder of the book appears to take a sharp turn away from the paradigm of the agent and index that has received such concerted attention thus far. It tackles the question of familial relations among artworks, and seems to shift back to conventional ground, in engaging with the concept of style. Yet this discussion, which proceeds via a rich formal analysis of the extraordinary corpus of Marquesan art documented by the German ethnologist Karl von den Steinen, is in the end consistent with what comes before.

zh: 盖尔再次着力避免“风格语法”之类的语言学模型，转而寻求通过对纹样之间生成关系的严格形式分析来找出纹样彼此连贯的轴线。本章大部分内容是对这些关系的富于视觉性的分析。双面雅努斯形象（几乎遍布大洋洲艺术）标示着不可侵犯性，这一点在《以影像包裹》中已经提出；关键不仅在于形象能朝所有方向观看，更在于面孔本身就是权力的表达，而且在雕塑形式中，它通常是神的面孔而非人的面孔。《以影像包裹》的一个核心主张是，东波利尼西亚纹身是一种强化身体的技术，而在马克萨斯群岛那种高度竞争、不稳定且暴力的社会中，纹身意味着身体面孔的倍增，这并不令人意外。这些主题对盖尔讨论马克萨斯形式——例如著名的乌乌（u'u）棍棒，本书称之为“终极的双重双重提基”——极为切题，但本章远远超出了早先对这些社会中赋能艺术的讨论。在这里，真正的目标是辨明赋予马克萨斯艺术以独特性的形式原则，而这些原则不是在外观层面被识别的，而是通过联结马克萨斯艺术品的那些变换类型被识别的。
en: Gell is again concerned to avoid linguistic models such as ‘a grammar of style' and instead seeks rather to identify axes of coherence through a strictly formal analysis of generative relations among motifs. The bulk of the chapter consists of a richly visual analysis of these relations. The point that Janus figures (which are almost pervasive in Oceanic art) indexed invulnerability had already been made in Wrapping in Images; it was not simply that the figure could see in all directions, but that the face was itself an expression of power, and, in sculptural form, was canonically the face of a deity rather than a human. One of the central claims of Wrapping in Images was that eastern Polynesian tattooing was a technology that reinforced the body, and in the highly competitive, unstable, and violent societies of the Marquesas, it is not unexpected to find that tattooing entailed the multiplication of the body's faces. These themes are highly salient to Gell's discussion of Marquesan forms such as the famous u'u clubs, described here as ‘the ultimate double-double tiki', but the chapter goes well beyond the earlier discussions of the arts of empowerment in these societies. The real object, in this case, is the diagnosis of the formal principles that give Marquesan art its singularity, and these are identified, not at the level of appearance, but through the types of transformations that link Marquesan artworks.

zh: 在最抽象的层面上，支配这些变换的原则可以与文化环境相联系。盖尔提出，在这批马克萨斯艺术材料中可以辨认出的最基本原则是一种“最小差异”原则：“纹样与形象所采取的形式，是在足以确立彼此区别的前提下，对相邻纹样改动最小的那些形式。”他声称，这一倾向反过来又可以与马克萨斯社会中身份形成的最基本特征相联系，该社会以激烈的地位竞争为特征；这不仅仅是政治上的角逐，而是一个被仪式浸透的个体间接触与共食的过程。人格的完整性不断受到弥散与去分化的威胁；许多马克萨斯人工制品单独来看就是包裹身体、保护特定孔窍或在危机情境中保护整个身体的装置；就整体组合而言，最小差异原则与一种对持续受威胁的分化努力、对消解之中进行分化的执着相呼应。“在人工制品领域的一种运作方式——通过插入微小变异从其他纹样生成纹样——与社会领域的一种运作方式——在融合性的同一背景上任意制造‘差异’——之间，存在着一种选择亲和性。”
en: At the most abstract level, the principles that govern these transformations can be connected to the cultural milieu. Gell suggests that the most basic principle to be detected in the Marquesan corpus is a principle of ‘least difference': ‘the forms taken by motifs and figures are the ones involving the least modification of neighbouring motifs consistent with the establishment of a distinction between them.' This trend can in turn, he claims, be connected with the most basic feature of identity-formation in Marquesan society, which was characterized by acute status competition; this was not simply a matter of political jockeying, but rather a ritually saturated process of inter-individual contact and commensality. Personal integrity was continually threatened by dispersal and de-differentiation; many Marquesan artefacts amounted, individually, to devices that wrapped the body and protected particular orifices, or the body as a whole in situations of crisis; in the ensemble as a whole, the principle of least difference resonated with a preoccupation with a continually prejudiced effort of differentiation, of differentiation in the midst of dissolution. ‘There was an elective affinity between a modus operandi in the artefactual domain, which generated motifs from other motifs by interpolating minuscule variations, and a modus operandi in the social realm which created "differences" arbitrarily against a background of fusional sameness.'

zh: 值得强调这一努力与艾伦·汉森的努力之间的区别，盖尔在本章开头一节认为后者虽有价值却构想有误。汉森试图在毛利艺术的形式属性（如被打断的对称）与毛利文化的属性（竞争性互惠）之间识别一一对应关系，盖尔则指出，被挑出来的那些风格元素是普遍的，或至少是常见的，因此不可能由毛利文化的独特特征所决定。尽管他试图在马克萨斯风格与文化之间识别的“选择亲和性”，可以说类似于汉森所设定的毛利审美形式与文化之间的复现关系，但对盖尔而言，亲和性不会出现在特定一批材料内部各项特征关系的层面，而是出现在“关系之间的关系”的层面；换言之，出现在那些可证明使该风格独具一格的元属性的层面。
en: It is worth underlining the distinction between this effort and that of Allan Hanson, which Gell finds, in an opening section of the chapter, to be worthy but misconceived. Whereas Hanson attempted to identify one-to-one correspondences between formal properties in Maori art (such as disrupted symmetry) and properties of Maori culture (competitive reciprocity), Gell points out that the stylistic elements that are singled out are universal, or at least commonly encountered, and cannot therefore be determined by singular features of Maori culture. Although the ‘elective affinity' that he seeks to identify between Marquesan style and culture could be seen to be similar to the relation of recapitulation that Hanson postulated between Maori aesthetic form and culture, for Gell the affinities will emerge not at the level of characteristic relations in particular bodies of material but at that of ‘relations between relations'; at the level, in other words, of meta-properties that demonstrably render that style peculiar to itself.

zh: 最后一章迈出了进一步的、同样雄心勃勃的一步，踏入一片常常被不尽如人意地涉足的领域，即那个通常被表述为个体心智与意识拥有何种集体对应物的问题。盖尔处理这一问题的方式之所以可能新颖而富有成效，恰恰是因为它不从通常的出发点起步，而是建立在前面若干论证之上——“内”与“外”、内部与外部，已经被表明是相对而非绝对对立的。受培尔·金特的洋葱、斯特拉森的分形人格观，以及波利尼西亚尤其是马克萨斯艺术中分形与分布式人格的非凡例证的启发，盖尔通过这样一个论证唤起了“分布式心智”的概念：“艺术史的结构展示了一种外在化、集体化的认知过程。”新爱尔兰著名的马兰甘与巴布亚新几内亚马辛地区的库拉交易被援引来推进这一论证，尤其借助南希·芒恩的研究表明，库拉操盘者“是一个在时空上延展的人”。在这一点上，本书的两个关键主题——分布式心智，以及有效力的能动性（本书开篇各节对此极为强调）——被汇聚到一起。效力建立在对外部场域的一个全面的内部模型之上。换言之，一个人之所以成为伟大的库拉操盘者，是因为他在心中构造出一个能够运转的拟像，一幅关于库拉在世间的运作与历史的动态时空地图。内部心智过程与对象化人格的外部交易（理想地）融为一体。因此，心智既可以主观地存在，也可以客观地存在，作为可交易对象的一种模式。
en: The final chapter makes a further, equally ambitious step, on to ground that has often been unsatisfactorily traversed, the problem that has been conventionally posed in terms of what collective counterparts individual minds and consciousnesses possess. Gell's approach to the issue may be fresh and rewarding precisely because it does not start from the usual departure points, but rather builds on several preceding arguments--‘inner' and ‘outer', internal and external, have already been shown to be relatively rather than absolutely contrasted. Inspired by Peer Gynt's onion, by Strathern's fractal conception of personhood, and by the extraordinary exemplification of fractal and distributed personhood in Polynesian and especially Marquesan art, Gell evokes the notion of a ‘distributed mind' through an argument that ‘the structures of art history demonstrate an externalized and collectivized cognitive process.' The famous Malangan of New Ireland and the Kula transactions of the Massim region of Papua New Guinea are invoked to advance this argument, demonstrating, with the support of the work of Nancy Munn in particular, that the Kula operator ‘is a spatio-temporally extended person'. At this point two of the book's key themes, that of the distributed mind, and that of efficacious agency-upon which so much emphasis is placed in the opening sections of the book-are drawn together. Efficacy is founded on a comprehensive internal model of the outside field. One becomes a great Kula operator, in other words, by modelling a working simulacrum, a dynamic space-time map, of the play and history of Kula in the world. Internal mental process and external transactions in objectified personhood are (ideally) fused. Mind, therefore, can exist objectively as well as subjectively, as a pattern of transactable objects.

zh: 盖尔并未以这一宏大主张作结，而是进而通过个体艺术家的创作（以西方艺术家为典型）这一更熟悉的实例来证成分布式心智的概念，同时也转而处理历时连续性问题，并预示了结尾关于传统问题的讨论。他在这里的关键术语是“前摄”（protention）与“滞留”（retention），二者指的是艺术品同时预期未来作品并回溯其他作品的方式。他的关键例子是杜尚的全部创作，尤其是“停顿之网”这一极为醒目的概念，它不仅启发了盖尔对这一问题的理解，也启发了他呈现这一问题时所采用的图示形式。本书最后一节回到集体层面，主张在毛利会堂的历史中可以识别出类似的前摄与滞留模式，从而把历史上形成的这一组会堂理解为“一个在结构上与作为时间过程的意识同构的分布式对象”。这一讨论有许多附带的成就，例如表明了“分形人格”——一个在美拉尼西亚人类学研究中形成且主要用于这一领域的概念——在该领域之外也有多大的解释力。
en: Gell does not conclude with this large claim, but proceeds to vindicate the concept of the distributed mind through the more familiar instance of the individual (canonically Western) artist's work, turning also to engage with questions of continuity over time, and foreshadowing the concluding discussion of questions of tradition. His key terms here are ‘protention' and ‘retention', which advert to the ways artworks at once anticipate future works and hark back to others. His key example is the œuvre of Duchamp, and particularly the very striking notion of ‘the network of stoppages' which inspired not only Gell's understanding of the issue, but the diagrammatic form in which he presents it. The final section of the book reverts to the collective register, arguing that a similar pattern of protentions and retentions can be identified in the history of Maori meeting houses, therefore understanding this historical corpus as 'a distributed object structurally isomorphous to consciousness as a temporal process'. There are many incidental accomplishments of this discussion, such as the demonstration of the extent to which ‘fractal personhood', a concept fashioned and largely isolated within Melanesianist anthropology, possesses great salience beyond it.

zh: 这是一部对读者要求很高的书。书中详细讨论的例证范围之广令人屏息，所处理的一系列重大概念问题同样如此。它不可避免地会引发争议：许多艺术人类学家在符号学解释上已展现出高超技艺，他们无疑仍不会相信，一种摒弃语言学类比与概念的进路能够比他们自己的进路更进一步。区域专家，例如波利尼西亚研究者，可能会对盖尔观看方式的出人意料感到吃惊。然而，他的挑战性观点无疑能催生新的研究。他关于大洋洲及其他材料的具体主张，使专家有机会超越那些已沦为通行之见、往往平淡无味的解释；而从艺术理论的视角出发对人格与认知根本问题加以理论化的这一前所未有的努力，对前者与对后者可能同样具有颠覆性与启发性。朋友与同事们仍痛苦地意识到，我们已失去与阿尔弗雷德本人进一步辩论这些问题的机会；然而他给我们留下了他自身人格的一个分布式要素，一个他自身创造技艺的索引，一份礼物。
en: This is a demanding book. The range of the examples that are discussed in detail is quite breath-taking, as is the ensemble of big conceptual questions that are tackled. It will inevitably be contentious: many anthropologists of art have exhibited great virtuosity in semiotic interpretations, and will no doubt remain unpersuaded that an approach which eschews linguistic analogies and concepts can represent an advance on their own. Regional specialists, such as Polynesianists, may be taken aback by the unexpected character of Gell's way of seeing. Yet the fertility of his provocation cannot be questioned. His specific claims concerning Oceanic and other materials give specialists a chance to move beyond the interpretations, too often bland interpretations, that have assumed the status of received wisdom; while the unprecedented effort to theorize fundamental questions of personhood and cognition from the vantage point of a theory of art may be as destabilizing and suggestive for the former as for the latter. Friends and colleagues remain painfully conscious of our lost opportunities to debate the issues further with Alfred in person; yet he has left us with a distributed element of his own personhood, an index of his own creative virtuosity, a gift.
